summary: A persistent, in-page status message. Intent picks the ARIA role for you.
useWhen: the message belongs to the page and should stay until the condition clears
form-level validation summaries, permission notices, degraded-state banners

useInstead.when: the message is transient and self-dismissing
useInstead.why: an Alert stays in the layout; a Toast does not

useInstead.when: it labels a value inline rather than telling the user something
useInstead.why: Badge shares Alert's intent vocabulary exactly, so a status mapped to one passes to the other

error.use: something failed and the user must act

warning.use: something may fail or has degraded

information.use: neutral context the user did not ask for

subtle.use: the default — tinted surface, readable in long pages

solid.use: reserve for a single high-stakes banner; it dominates the layout

inline.use: inside a form or card, in the flow of content

banner.use: full-bleed at the top of a page or region

guarantees: the role follows the intent — error and warning are role=alert, everything else role=status
the icon is aria-hidden, so the live region announces the text once and not the glyph
requires: `dismissLabel` when `onDismiss` is set and the surrounding copy does not name the action
notes: role=alert interrupts whatever the screen reader is saying; role=status waits for a pause. This is why the role is not a prop.

antiPatterns.dont: using intent="error" for a message that is merely informational
antiPatterns.why: error renders role=alert, which interrupts the screen reader. A page of interrupting status messages talks over the user.

antiPatterns.dont: using intent="information" for a genuine failure
antiPatterns.why: role=status waits for a pause, so a real error can be missed entirely

antiPatterns.dont: rendering an Alert conditionally for a transient confirmation
antiPatterns.why: an Alert that appears and disappears shifts the layout under the user
